Metadata.title: Ondivento — wind-optimized bike routes
Metadata.description: A cycling route planner that uses the hour-by-hour wind forecast to decide where to ride and when to leave. Built for Tierra de Campos, Spain.

Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.whoBody: Ondivento is a personal project by Daniel Paniagua. For any question, or to exercise your rights over your data, write to <mail></mail>.
Privacy.noAccountTitle: Planning a route neither asks for nor stores your identity
Privacy.noAccountBody: This comes first because it's what actually matters: you can plan routes, see the forecast and export the GPX without creating an account. The start point, the distance and the route coordinates are sent to our server only to work out the route, and passed on to the map and weather providers listed below — they aren't stored in any database tied to you. Your rider profile (height, weight, FTP, bike) stays in your own browser, not on our servers, unless you decide to create an account. The one exception is pressing "Share": that deliberately stores a copy of that route, because it's exactly what makes the link work. It's explained in full below.
Privacy.accountIntro: The account is optional and exists to carry your profile, your bikes and your routes from one device to another. When you create it we store:
Privacy.accountIdentity: Basic identity: your email, and if you sign in with Google, your name and profile picture as Google passes them to us. If you sign in by email link, just your address.
Privacy.accountProfile: Rider profile: height, weight, FTP and intensity factor.
Privacy.accountBikes: Bikes: name and components (frame, wheels, tyres...) to work out their aerodynamics. None of this identifies anyone on its own.
Privacy.accountRoutes: Saved routes: name, distance and the coordinates of the track.
Privacy.accountAlerts: Wind alerts: if you turn on alerts for a route, we store that you want them, when you were last alerted (so we don't repeat ourselves) and the language you were using the app in, so we can write to you in it.
Privacy.accountDelete: You can delete each bike or route individually from the app itself, and switch alerts off under "My routes". To delete the whole account, write to <mail></mail> — there's no self-service button for that yet.
Privacy.thirdTitle: What third parties receive, and why
Privacy.thirdIntro: Ondivento doesn't exist without leaning on external services. Each one receives only what it needs to do its part:
Privacy.thirdGeo: Open-Meteo, OpenRouteService, BRouter and OSRM receive coordinates to work out the wind and the route — never your identity, not even if you have an account.
Privacy.thirdGoogle: Google, if you choose that way in, to confirm who you are.
Privacy.thirdResend: Resend to send the sign-in link and, if you turn them on, the wind alerts.
Privacy.thirdCarto: CARTO serves the map tiles; it receives the coordinates shown on screen, like any web map.
Privacy.thirdVercel: Vercel hosts the application and, like any server, sees the IP of whoever uses it in its technical access logs. It also collects aggregated, anonymous usage statistics.
Privacy.cookiesBody: Only the strictly functional ones: the session cookie, to keep you signed in if you have an account, and the language one, to remember whether you prefer Spanish or English. No advertising, no cross-site tracking.
Privacy.rightsBody: Access, rectification, portability and erasure of your data, under the GDPR. Write to <mail></mail> and it's handled directly, with no middlemen — this is one person's project, not a company with a support department.
Privacy.shareIntro: Sharing doesn't require an account. Pressing "Share" stores a frozen copy of that route on our server and generates a link. Without that copy, whoever opened it would see a different route, because the wind would have changed.
Privacy.shareWhat: What's stored: the route's name, its coordinates, the distance and the climbing. Nothing about you. If you have an account we also record that it was yours, so you can recognise it.
Privacy.shareWho: Who can see it: anyone with the link. The identifier is long and random, so it can't be guessed by trying, and shared routes aren't listed or indexed anywhere — but if you pass the link on, whoever gets it can pass it on too. Treat it as public.
Privacy.shareCare: Think twice if it starts at your house. A route's start point says a fair bit about where you live. Sharing one that begins at your front door is your call, but it's better to know that beforehand than afterwards.
Privacy.shareDelete: How long it lasts: it doesn't expire on its own, so a link you sent months ago still works. If you want a shared route deleted, write to with the link and it'll be removed.

Terms.title: Terms of use
Terms.intro: Ondivento is a personal project, free, made by one person. These terms are short on purpose.
Terms.estimateTitle: It's an estimate, not a promise
Terms.estimateBody: The times, the wind and the surface come from models and weather forecasts — never from a measurement taken right now. The three-day forecast is indicative; beyond that, it's less reliable still. The paved/unpaved split depends on what OpenStreetMap has tagged on each stretch, which isn't always complete or up to date. Use your own judgement on the road: the actual conditions, the traffic and how you're feeling always outrank whatever the app says.
Terms.availabilityBody: It leans on free external services (OpenRouteService, BRouter, OSRM, Open-Meteo) that have their own limits and outages. The app tries to switch from one to another when one fails, but the service isn't guaranteed to be available at all times.
Terms.accountTitle: Your account, if you make one
Terms.accountBody: It's free and optional. You can stop using it whenever you like and ask for your data to be deleted by writing to <mail>privacidad@ondivento.com</mail>. More detail on what's stored and why is on the <privacy>privacy page</privacy>.
Terms.fairUseBody: Route planning depends on a quota shared with free external services. Please don't automate bulk requests against the application — there's a technical limit that cuts off abuse, but we'd rather not need it.
Terms.changesBody: If anything relevant changes in how data is handled, this page and the privacy page will be updated, with the date at the top.

Server.noOrsKey: No OpenRouteService key: routing falls back to free public servers. It works fine, but it can't report the paved/unpaved split and may get busy at peak times.
Server.noPavedLoop: There's no loop of that distance from there without touching some track: the best one is {pct}% unpaved.
Server.noElevation: No elevation data: the times ignore the hills.
Server.tooManyPlans: Too many routes in a row. Give it a moment before planning again.
Server.tooManySearches: Too many searches in a row.
Server.missingEnd: A point-to-point route needs a finish point
Server.badDistance: The distance must be between 5 and 400 km
Server.routersSlow: The routing servers are taking too long. Try again, or with a shorter distance.
Server.analyzeSlow: The analysis took too long. Try a shorter route.
Server.needTwoPoints: The route needs at least two points
Server.tooManyPoints: The route has too many points
Server.mustSignIn: You need to sign in first
Server.tooManyRoutes: You already have 200 saved routes. Delete one first.
Server.weatherRateLimited: The weather service is rate-limiting requests. Wait a minute and try again.
Server.tooManyShares: Too many shared routes in a row. Give it a moment.
Server.shareUnavailable: Sharing isn't available on this deployment.

Rider.title: Rider profile
Rider.subtitle: The better you tune it, the closer the times will be to your own.
Rider.bsaExplainer: Your height and weight give your body surface area (Du Bois) and from that the area you offer to the air: <n>{bsa} m²</n> of surface, <n>{body} m²</n> of body CdA.
Rider.intensityExplainer: What fraction of your FTP you plan to hold on average. For a long ride 0.65–0.75 is normal; above 0.85 you only last an hour or two.

Install.android: Install it and you get it as an app: no browser bar, and it opens with no signal.

Import.orTap: or tap to browse · GPX, TCX or KML
Import.blurb: Export the route from Strava, Komoot or Garmin and I'll tell you what time to ride it and in which direction. The file is read in your browser; only the coordinates go to the server.
Import.noTrack: I couldn't find a track inside. GPX, TCX and KML with route points all work.
